I'm working on the TODO for LinearAlgebra.TensorPower.Symmetric which is:

  • Grading: show that there is a map Sym[R]^i M × Sym[R]^j M → Sym[R]^(i + j) M that is
    associative and commutative, and that n ↦ Sym[R]^n M is a graded (semi)ring and algebra.
  • Universal property: linear maps from Sym[R]^n M to N correspond to symmetric multilinear
    maps M ^ n to N.
  • Relate to homogeneous (multivariate) polynomials of degree n.

I've basically done the Universal property. see #mathlib4 > SymmetricPower universal property

I've thought more about the multivariate polynomial story, but have not thought as much about the first item in the list.

But: as far as I can tell, this architecture doesn't quite match what is currently done with the TensorAlgebra. What I mean is that TensorAlgebra R M does not seem to be defined as (or even identified with) n -> TensorPower R n M. Have I overlooked something?

For what it is worth, my motivating interest in working on this came about because I wanted "coordinate free" descriptions of homogeneous forms -- i.e. essentially SymmetricPower iota M and I wanted to be able to relate these to MvPolynomials (basically the third TODO item, which will depend on using the universal property).

On the other hand, I'm happy to work on the first item -- just wanted to understand the big picture directions a bit before proceeding.

From just the math POV, my take is that it would be nice to have SymmetricAlgebra defined as a quotient of TensorAlgebra.

And TensorAlgebra should have a grading with summands the TensorPowers -- i.e. an identification of TensorAlgebra R M with n -> TensorPower R n M.

Then also SymmetricAlgebra should have a grading with summands the SymmetricPowers. But maybe there are reasons to proceed otherwise?

George McNinch said:

it would be nice to have docs#SymmetricAlgebra defined as a quotient of docs#TensorAlgebra.

Isn't it already how it's defined?

Sorry - yes, I forgot for a moment. The way the TODO is phrased sounded close to creating a ring structure on n -> SymmetricPower R n M (also: should be "finitely supported function" arrow of course...)

I guess from this point of view, the TODO amounts to describing the multiplication of homogeneous elements in SymmetricAlgebra.

Maybe one thing I need to understand better is the analogous results forTensorPowers giving a grading on TensorAlgebra.

George McNinch said:

or even identified with

@loogle TensorAlgebra, TensorPower
:search: TensorPower.toTensorAlgebra, TensorAlgebra.equivDirectSum, and 15 more

We have an ongoing PR #36501 with @María Inés de Frutos Fernández that does gradings of quotients of graded algebras by homogeneous relations / ideals. It works but @Eric Wieser made us observe that it could be shorter.
